staples.name: Milk
staples.notes: Any fat level (skim/1%/2%/whole).

staples.name: Soy milk, calcium-fortified
staples.notes: Counts as dairy only if calcium-fortified (check label). Almond/oat/rice milk do NOT count as dairy.

staples.name: Greek yogurt, plain
staples.notes: Single-serve cup. Flavored Greek cups count the same for dairy.

staples.name: Yogurt, plain (regular)
staples.notes: Regular (non-Greek) yogurt is actually higher in calcium than Greek (~400 mg/cup per USDA); rules-table value used.

staples.name: Yogurt, flavored cup
staples.notes: Fruit-on-the-bottom/flavored single cup; fruit in it is too little to count.

staples.name: Kefir
staples.notes: Supermarket kefir is pasteurized; unpasteurized/raw-milk kefir would need unpasteurized_dairy.

staples.name: Cheddar cheese
staples.notes: 1.5 oz natural cheese = 1 cup eq. Shredded: ¼ cup ≈ 1 oz.

staples.name: Cottage cheese
staples.notes: 2 cups cottage cheese = 1 cup eq dairy, so it counts little toward dairy despite the protein.

staples.name: Parmesan, grated
staples.notes: Hard cheese by weight: 0.35 oz / 1.5 oz. Supermarket parmesan is pasteurized.

staples.name: Egg
staples.notes: Boiled, poached or fried without counted oil; cook until yolk is firm.

staples.name: Eggs, scrambled (2 eggs + 1 tsp oil)
staples.notes: If scrambled in butter instead of oil, oils = 0. Cook until no liquid egg remains.

staples.name: Apple
staples.notes: Rules: 1 medium ≈ 1 cup eq; a small apple ≈ ½.

staples.name: Clementine
staples.notes: ~74 g each; about 2½ clementines ≈ 1 cup.

staples.name: Berries
staples.notes: Fresh or frozen.

staples.name: Cut fruit / melon
staples.notes: Watermelon, cantaloupe, honeydew, pineapple or a mixed fruit cup. Pre-cut fruit: keep refrigerated, eat promptly.

staples.name: Mango
staples.notes: A whole mango ≈ 2 cups; log 2 servings.

staples.name: Raisins
staples.notes: ½ cup dried fruit = 1 cup eq. A mini snack box (0.5 oz) ≈ ⅓ of this.

staples.name: Orange juice, 100%
staples.notes: Supermarket juice is pasteurized. Fresh-squeezed/unpasteurized juice → unpasteurized_juice.

staples.name: Orange juice, calcium-fortified
staples.notes: Calcium per label (typically 300–350 mg/cup). Doesn't count as dairy.

staples.name: Sourdough bread
staples.notes: Bakery slices run 1–2 oz; a thin sandwich-style slice = 1 oz eq.

staples.name: Oatmeal, cooked
staples.notes: Made with water. If cooked in milk, also log the milk.

staples.name: Instant oatmeal packet
staples.notes: Most instant packets are calcium-fortified (~100 mg); plain/unfortified ≈ 20 mg. Made with water.

staples.name: Cereal, whole-grain (Cheerios-type)
staples.notes: Dry cereal only; log the milk separately. Calcium varies by brand fortification.

staples.name: Cereal, refined (corn flakes/Rice Krispies-type)
staples.notes: Dry cereal only; log the milk separately.

staples.name: Granola
staples.notes: Typical nut-containing granola (~60 g). Brands vary a lot; dense ½ cup.

staples.name: Pasta
staples.notes: Plain pasta only; log sauce/cheese separately.

staples.name: Bagel, plain
staples.notes: Large bagel = 4 oz eq; a packaged (Thomas'-type) bagel ≈ 3, a mini ≈ 1. Whole-wheat bagel → treat as grain_whole.

staples.name: Flour tortilla
staples.notes: 6-inch = 1 oz eq, 8-inch ≈ 2, 10-inch burrito ≈ 4.

staples.name: Corn tortillas
staples.notes: Whole-grain corn per rules.

staples.name: Crackers
staples.notes: Saltines have less oil (~1.5 g), butter-type rounds more (~5 g); averaged.

staples.name: Popcorn
staples.notes: Assumes lightly oiled/'light' microwave. Air-popped: oils 0; regular microwave/movie popcorn has more (largely palm, not counted).

staples.name: Rice cakes
staples.notes: By weight: 18 g / 28 g. Plain brown-rice cakes are whole grain.

staples.name: Hot oats, 1.5 servings + 1 slice whole-wheat bread
staples.notes: Anny's usual: 1.5 package servings of oats (serving = ½ cup dry) + 1 slice whole-wheat toast. Oats made with water; log milk, nut butter, fruit separately.

staples.name: Chia seeds
staples.notes: By weight (½ oz seeds = 1 oz eq); chia is denser than the 2-tbsp rule of thumb.

staples.name: Hummus
staples.notes: Bean-part estimate per rules (~60% chickpeas). MyPlate's shortcut (2 tbsp hummus = 1 oz eq protein) would give 0.5 cup eq legumes.

staples.name: Tofu, firm
staples.notes: Calcium assumes calcium-set tofu (calcium sulfate on label); nigari-set ≈ 100 mg.

staples.name: Edamame, shelled
staples.notes: Edamame counts as soy (protein), not legume vegetable, per rules.

staples.name: Chicken breast
staples.notes: Cook to 165°F.

staples.name: Ground beef
staples.notes: Cook to 160°F (no pink). Beef fat is not counted as oil.

staples.name: Meat, card-deck portion
staples.notes: Anny's visual reference: palm-size / deck-of-cards piece of cooked chicken, beef or pork ≈ 3 oz.

staples.name: Salmon
staples.notes: Low-mercury. Cook to 145°F. Cold-smoked lox is a separate case (smoked_seafood).

staples.name: Tuna, canned light
staples.notes: Water-packed. A 5-oz can drains to ~4 oz. Light tuna is low-mercury; albacore is tracked separately.

staples.name: Tuna, canned albacore
staples.notes: Albacore counts in seafood AND the albacore weekly cap (FDA: ≤ 4 oz/week).

staples.name: Salmon, canned with bones
staples.notes: Mash the soft bones in — that's where the calcium is.

staples.name: Shrimp
staples.notes: Cook until opaque; no raw shrimp/ceviche.

staples.name: Deli turkey, heated
staples.notes: Flagged deli_meat: fine if heated to steaming (165°F) right before eating.

staples.name: Beef jerky
staples.notes: Dried meat is concentrated: 1 oz ≈ 1.5 oz eq. Commercial shelf-stable jerky is cooked during processing, so not flagged; avoid homemade/refrigerated deli-style jerky. High sodium.

staples.name: Salad greens
staples.notes: 2 cups raw leafy = 1 cup eq. Iceberg/butter lettuce → veg_other instead. Log dressing separately. Rinse bagged greens.

staples.name: Spinach, cooked
staples.notes: Spinach calcium is poorly absorbed (oxalate); value is USDA content.

staples.name: Broccoli
staples.notes: Raw florets: same cup eq, choline ~17 mg.

staples.name: Bell pepper, red
staples.notes: Green bell pepper → veg_other.

staples.name: Snap peas
staples.notes: Edible-pod peas are 'other' veg; shelled green peas would be starchy.

staples.name: Sweet potato
staples.notes: MyPlate: 1 large baked sweet potato = 1 cup; medium ≈ ¾.

staples.name: Baked potato
staples.notes: Toppings (butter, sour cream, cheese) logged separately.

staples.name: Corn on the cob
staples.notes: Large ear (8–9 in) = 1 cup.

staples.name: Vegetable soup
staples.notes: Broth-based mixed-vegetable soup, ~½ cup veg per cup. Bean soups/minestrone have legumes — log as a recipe if possible.

staples.name: Mayonnaise
staples.notes: Commercial mayo uses pasteurized eggs. Homemade mayo/aioli with raw yolk → raw_egg.

staples.name: Butter
staples.notes: Solid fat: not counted as oil per rules.

staples.name: Vinaigrette / salad dressing
staples.notes: Bottled vinaigrette ≈ 10 g oil per 2 tbsp; homemade 3:1 vinaigrette ≈ 20 g. Creamy dressings similar.

staples.name: Trail mix
staples.notes: Assumes nuts + raisins + a few chocolate candies.

staples.name: Granola bar
staples.notes: Chewy/crunchy oat bar. A crunchy 2-bar pouch ≈ 1 oz eq whole grain. Protein bars differ — log separately.

staples.name: Dark chocolate
staples.notes: Cocoa butter is a solid fat (not counted). ~20–25 mg caffeine per oz.

staples.name: Smoothie, fruit + yogurt
staples.notes: Homemade: ½ cup yogurt + ½ cup milk + 1 cup fruit. Shop smoothies made with juice/sherbet have less dairy.

staples.name: Latte
staples.notes: ~75 mg caffeine (1 shot) toward the 200 mg/day limit. Oat/almond milk lattes: dairy 0; soy only if calcium-fortified.

staples.name: Pizza, cheese
staples.notes: Large-pizza slice; thin crust ≈ 1.5 oz eq grain.
